Make a game that, if everyone played it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Build this as a complete, playable Godot 4.7.2 project in the current directory.
- Use the gl_compatibility renderer, and don't enable thread support (it must run as a web export).
- Set a main scene in project.godot. Add a short README.md with run instructions.
- Keep it self-contained: no downloads, external assets or plugins.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory. Don't export the project; that happens afterwards.
- Check it loads: run `godot --headless --path . --editor --quit` and fix any errors.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

I'll build **Ripple**, a game that trains people to spot misinformation. It's based on "psychological inoculation" research, which has some of the strongest evidence of any intervention that scales: when people practise spotting manipulation techniques in a safe setting, they get better at resisting them in real life. The game also teaches players to recognise and share honest information, so they don't just learn to distrust everything.

func _button(text: String, color: Color, font_color := INK_COLOR, font_size := 18) -> Button:

	b.text = text
	b.focus_mode = FOCUS_NONE
	b.mouse_default_cursor_shape = CURSOR_POINTING_HAND
	b.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", font_size)
	b.add_theme_stylebox_override("normal", _style(color, 10, 10))
	b.add_theme_stylebox_override("hover", _style(color.lightened(0.18), 10, 10))
	b.add_theme_stylebox_override("pressed", _style(color.darkened(0.15), 10, 10))
	b.add_theme_stylebox_override("focus", StyleBoxEmpty.new())
	for k in ["font_color", "font_hover_color", "font_pressed_color", "font_focus_color", "font_hover_pressed_color"]:

	b.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, 50)

func evaluate(choice: String) -> void:
	if state != "choose" and state != "pick":
		return
	state = "feedback"
	var answer: String = current.a
	var also: Array = current.get("also", [])
	var outcome := ""
	if answer == "honest":
		outcome = "honest_shared" if choice == "honest" else "honest_flagged"
	elif choice == "honest":
		outcome = "trick_shared"
	elif choice == answer or also.has(choice):
		outcome = "trick_named"
	else:
		outcome = "trick_caught"

	var correct := outcome == "honest_shared" or outcome == "trick_named"
	total_seen += 1
	chapter_seen += 1
	stats[answer][1] += 1
	if correct:
		total_correct += 1
		chapter_correct += 1
		stats[answer][0] += 1
		streak += 1
		best_streak = maxi(best_streak, streak)
	elif outcome != "trick_caught":
		streak = 0

	var info: Dictionary = Content.TECHNIQUES.get(answer, {})
	var why: String = current.why
	var title := ""
	var color := HONEST_COLOR
	var impact := ""
	match outcome:
		"honest_shared":
			title = "Good share! This one was honest."
			impact = "You passed on useful information, and your neighbours are better informed."
			town.send_wave(0.11)
		"trick_named":
			title = "Spotted it: " + info.name
			color = Color(info.color)
			impact = "You stopped it spreading and helped your neighbours learn the trick too."
			if choice != answer:
				title = "Spotted it: " + Content.TECHNIQUES[choice].name
				why = "Its main trick is %s. %s" % [info.name, why]
			town.send_wave(0.13)
		"trick_caught":
			title = "You caught it, but the main trick is " + info.name
			color = ALERT_COLOR
			impact = "You stopped it spreading. Naming the right trick helps people recognise it next time."
			town.send_wave(0.05)
		"trick_shared":
			title = "Oops! That was a trick: " + info.name
			color = BAD_COLOR
			impact = "It spread fast. Misleading posts often travel further and faster than the truth."
			town.send_wave(-0.2)
		"honest_flagged":
			title = "Actually, this one was honest."
			color = BAD_COLOR
			impact = "Useful information didn't reach the people who needed it. Too much suspicion does harm too."
			town.send_wave(-0.12)
	fb_title.text = title
	fb_title.add_theme_color_override("font_color", color)
	fb_style.border_color = color
	fb_text.text = why
	if answer == "honest":
		fb_ask.text = Content.HONEST_SIGNS
	else:
		fb_ask.text = "Ask yourself:  " + info.question
	fb_impact.text = impact
	fb_panel.reset_size()
	_show_actions("feedback")
	_update_top()

	card_style.border_color = color
	stamp.text = "SHARED" if choice == "honest" else "FLAGGED"
	stamp_style.bg_color = Color(color, 0.95)
	stamp.add_theme_color_override("font_color", INK_COLOR)
	stamp.visible = true
	stamp.reset_size()
	stamp.pivot_offset = stamp.size * 0.5
	stamp.position = CARD_HOME + Vector2(470, 70)
	stamp.rotation = -0.18
	stamp.scale = Vector2(1.8, 1.8)
	stamp.modulate.a = 0.0
	var tw := create_tween().set_parallel(true)
	tw.tween_property(stamp, "scale", Vector2.ONE, 0.22).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw.tween_property(stamp, "modulate:a", 1.0, 0.15)


func _on_continue() -> void:

		return
	post_idx += 1
	var ch: Dictionary = Content.CHAPTERS[chapter_idx]

		show_post()
		return
	chapter_idx += 1
	if chapter_idx < Content.CHAPTERS.size():
		show_intro()
	else:

func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if not (event is InputEventKey and event.pressed and not event.echo):
		return
	var k: Key = event.keycode
	var confirm := k == KEY_ENTER or k == KEY_KP_ENTER or k == KEY_SPACE
	match state:
		"title", "intro", "end":
			if confirm and overlay_action.is_valid():
				overlay_action.call()
		"choose", "pick":

# Ripple

*A game about what we share, and why it matters.*

You live in the small town of Brindlewick. Posts arrive in your feed one at a
time. For each one you decide whether to **share it**, or whether **something's
off**. If something's off, you name the manipulation trick it uses. Your choices
ripple out across a network of neighbours, making them clear-minded or leaving
them in the fog.

Over seven chapters you learn the six most common manipulation techniques:
**Emotional Bait, Fake Expert, False Choice, Scapegoat, Personal Attack and
Cherry-Picking**. Just as important, you learn to recognise honest information
(named sources, a calm tone, admitting what isn't known, correcting mistakes),
because too much suspicion does harm too.

## Why this game

Research on "psychological inoculation" (Roozenbeek, van der Linden and others)
has found that practising how to spot manipulation techniques in a safe setting
helps people resist them in real life. Misinformation affects health, elections
and how neighbours treat each other, so if everyone played this game, almost
everyone would benefit. The game takes about 15 minutes, needs no reading
beyond everyday language, and ends with a pocket guide of seven questions to
ask before sharing anything.

## Running

1. Install [Godot 4.7](https://godotengine.org/) (standard build).
2. Open this folder in Godot (Project Manager → Import → `project.godot`) and press **F5**,
   or run from a terminal: `godot --path .`

The project uses the GL Compatibility renderer with no threads, so it can be exported to the web.

## Controls

| Action | Mouse | Keyboard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Share a post | "Share it" | `S` |
| Flag a post | "Something's off" | `F` |
| Name the trick | Coloured buttons | `1`–`6` |
| Back | "Back" | `Esc` |
| Continue / start | Blue button | `Enter` / `Space` |
EOF

I've built **Ripple**, a complete Godot 4.7 game that teaches players to spot online misinformation. `godot --headless --path . --editor --quit` loads with no errors or warnings. An automated script also played through all 44 posts with no runtime errors (it got 36 right and ended with 37 of 42 neighbours clear-minded), and I checked the main screens from rendered screenshots.

**Why this game:** I chose to tackle misinformation because it affects nearly everyone: health choices, elections, and how neighbours treat each other. "Psychological inoculation" research (Roozenbeek, van der Linden and others) has found that practising how to spot manipulation techniques in a safe setting helps people resist them in real life. A short game with plain language and nothing that ties it to one culture could reach very large numbers of people.

**How it plays**
- You live in Brindlewick, a fictional town, so the game doesn't take sides in real politics. Posts appear one at a time: you either **share** the post or decide **something's off** and name the trick it uses.
- **Six chapters each teach one trick:** Emotional Bait, Fake Expert, False Choice, Scapegoat, Personal Attack and Cherry-Picking. A seventh chapter mixes them all together, and some posts there use more than one trick.
- **Honest posts are about a third of the feed, and flagging them costs you.** This is deliberate, so players learn to trust good sources rather than become cynical. Honest examples include a named doctor, a newspaper correction, a mayor admitting a mistake, and a lost cat.
- **Every answer explains why**, gives a question to ask yourself, and says what happened in town as a result.
- **The town is a network of 42 neighbours.** Each choice ripples out from "you" and turns them clear-minded (gold, smiling) or misled (grey, in fog). Lies spread harder than truth, so you need roughly 60% accuracy just to keep the town from getting worse.
- **Some posts link together:** an honest crime report ("2 thefts, up from 1") comes back later as "CRIME HAS DOUBLED!!!", and one fake account uses a 1 in place of an "l".
- **The end screen** shows your results and town outcome, plus a pocket guide of seven questions to ask before sharing anything.

It runs on the gl_compatibility renderer with no thread support and no external assets: all visuals are drawn in code. You can play with the mouse, or the keyboard (`S`, `F`, `1`–`6`, `Esc`, `Enter`). Text has no emoji, because they may not display in the web build.

**Files**
- `project.godot`: main scene is `main.tscn`, window is 1280×720
- `scripts/main.gd`: UI, game flow, scoring and feedback
- `scripts/town.gd`: the animated neighbour network
- `scripts/content.gd`: the techniques and all 44 posts
- `README.md`: how to run it, and controls
